# Independent audit of the actual normal Hessian and inside-transition example

I read the complete sources
\`candidate 8bc6ff090380166a\`
and
\`candidate be37e5b9b9c4c946\`.
The claims pass in their stated scope. This audit supplies no cap-mass or OC inference from the covariance inequality.

## 1. Full-normal derivative

Writing \(m_t=(N+tD)\cdot(w-Y)/\Gamma(u+tv)\) at \(\Gamma(u)=1\), the first derivative is \(k_D=D\cdot(w-Y)-\gamma_Dm\), and the second is \(-2\gamma_Dk_D-\eta_Dm\). Since \(\int m\psi/h=A-bS\), actual first-order normal stationarity reduces the second derivative to
\[
\int\psi'(q)k_D^2/h^2+(bS-A)\eta_D.
\]
The radial null direction and absence of a pure-base normalization term both check. Freezing the physical width would give a different, incorrect formula.

For the uniform kernel, its positive-part difference has lower-plane corner sign plus and upper-plane sign minus. A proper section has full central trace; a supporting facet has half the full central trace. The one-sided traces are the appropriate squared positive or negative part. This distinction is necessary and correctly retained.

## 2. Limit and selector checks

The nearby proper sections converge in their intrinsic section dimension. On a limiting supporting facet, homothety about a uniformly interior fiber point compares the two endpoint slices, so their ordered limits give the nonnegative transition density \(\chi\). Multiplication by \(h\) kills the bounded normalization correction. On the limiting plane \(m=-b\), the test \(k_D\) is exactly the affine incidence about \(Y-b(0,\Sigma u)\). Therefore the resulting PSD form tests no arbitrary constant function. Its correct strength is a covariance inequality, not total-mass domination.

The common height selector gives \(\tau=\min(1,(g)_+)\); on \(0<\tau<1\) its endpoint footprint difference has limit one, hence \(1_{\{0<\tau<1\}}\leq\chi\). At saturated limits the endpoint record remains independent, as the stated \(g_l=\pm1/l\) examples show.

The primitive \(J_1=-\Psi+\Psi^2/2\) satisfies \(J_1'=q\psi\). The outside trace is \(-\tau+\tau^2/2\), while subtraction of the full-volume constant on an inside face gives \(-\tau^2/2\). Thus the signed partial-capture identity and its factor \(1/(2|u|)\) are correct. Strong \(L^1\) selector convergence, not weak convergence alone, justifies the squared terms.

## 3. Exact inside-transition example

For the three intervals in the companion example, total mass is \(4\), within-fiber covariance is \((1+8+1)/(12\cdot4)=5/24\), and \(f_H\) at the middle center is \(1/2\). The interval energy formula \(E=L(1-(2t/L)^2)\) gives the displayed tied profile exactly.

At the proposed middle mark the positive-orientation paired outer kernel arguments sum to \(-1\), so their captures sum to one for every base tilt. The negative-orientation paired arguments have nonnegative sum and their captures sum to at least one. Finite saturation attains equality in that orientation. The own middle depth is uniquely maximal at its center, and the exposed endpoint source upper bounds are strictly smaller. Pure-base caps have mass at least three. These observations establish actual global uniqueness and the full ambient cap minimum, rather than only a selected menu equality.

Both retained supporting selectors equal \(1/2\), while both transition records equal one. The endpoint section moments at bases \(-1,+1\) cancel exactly. In dimension one the remaining continuous-normal direction is radial, so the displayed pure-base quadratic equality is the complete normal PSD test.

The example is above the OC target and is not claimed to be a body minimum. It correctly refutes only elimination of inside transitions from the stated cap-wise first/second-order information.

## 4. Required caution for any next use

A zero Hessian direction need not generate an interval of minimizing caps. Exact movable active families must follow from a separate identity, saturation chamber, or other global minimum argument. Conversely a positive or semidefinite section covariance does not by itself supply a sharp captured-volume payment.
